text.p: Mercedes-Benz of North America Inc said Wednesday it had set the base U.S. price of $33,950 on its 1998 ML320 sport utility vehicle.
The price does not include a $595 destination and handling charge. The vehicle, unveiled earliert this year, is built at Mercedes's first assembly plant outside Germany, in Vance, Ala.
The price is slightly less than Daimler-Benz AG Mercedes executives had hinted. They had said it would be priced in the mid-$30,000 range.
The ML320 will compete in the heart of the premium SUV segment, along with vehicles such as Ford Motor Co's Explorer Limited and Chrysler Corp's Jeep Grand Cherokee Limited models.
Mercedes spokeswoman Donna Boland said the company will begin its advertising launch for the six-cylinder ML320 in mid-September. It will be available at about 300 of Mercedes's 320 U.S. dealers.
Mercedes will offer only one option package and three stand-alone options at launch, bringing the maximum price to $40,115, including the destination charge.

A "premium" package -- including leather-trim (seats, steering wheel and gearshift knob), walnut dashboard and console trim, heated seats, auto-dimming rear-view mirror, additional instrumentation, lockable safebox and rear privacy glass -- is available for $2,950.
Individual options include power tilt/sliding tinted glass sunroof at $1,095, a Bose premium audio system at $1,050, and metallic paint at $475.

Standard features include a full-time four-wheel drive system with a 215-horsepower, 3.2-liter V6 engine, independent rear suspension, anti-lock disc brakes, anti-theft alarm, air conditioning with dust filter, power windows and locks, and other features.
Mercedes has said its Alabama plant will produce 60,000-65,000 vehicles a year once full production is reached next year, and will sell about half of the vehicles in the United States.
